public_rationale: He says there 'just doesn't seem to be the investor hunger' to buy a company valued at $9.9 billion. That is a hedged impression of buyer appetite. 'Hunger' has no measure, and interest in a company valued at $9.9B need not mean an offer at that price, so counting deals at that size would not test it fairly. Buyers clearly wanted Cursor by 2026 (SpaceX paid $60 billion), but that is a later period and does not show what appetite was in August 2025.
limitations: Private bids and talks from mid-2025 are mostly not public, so even a narrower test would rest on incomplete records.
